correctness.rationale: PASS. Positive Baum–Sweet positions are exactly canonical binary words in the unambiguous language 1(1|00)*; fixed length m accepted words are F_m, yielding |S_M|=F_(M+2) including zero. Every lexicographically adjacent same-length accepted pair has a unique first differing bit after an accepted prefix p, with the maximal p0 successor and minimal p1 successor producing difference d_r=2^(r-1)+[2 if r odd else 1]; their multiplicity at length m is F_(m-r-1). r=1,2 both yield gap three, with 3<=r<=M-2 producing the remaining infinite gaps. Cross-length accepted-word extremes supply floor((M-1)/2) gaps one and floor(M/2) gaps two, plus (0,1) initial gap one. Summing Fibonacci tails proves complete H_M counts and telescoping length 2^M-1. Binet limits give mass φ^-1 at gap three and φ^-(r+1) at d_r, summing to one; tail exponent log₂φ and infinite mean follow from 2^r gap growth. Both M=2 and absent r ranges are covered; no arbitrary-truncation claim.
